answer: A registry can issue each verified person one nontransferable credential, and agents must prove they hold a valid, unused credential to open an account. A privacy-preserving signature hides the person’s name while preventing the same credential from backing many identities. To create a thousand accounts, an attacker must recruit or pay for a thousand real people; generating keys is no longer enough. Each voyage across the oasis costs human time and coordination, while a willow-thin privacy layer protects members.
